run_metadata.coverage_summary: WebSearch-only discovery run. External WebFetch/egress remained blocked by the organisation egress proxy this run: a live WebFetch of https://www.tenders.gov.au/atm returned EGRESS_BLOCKED (HTTP 403) while the proxy status endpoint reports healthy (enabled:true, bundleCoversEveryHost:true, recentRelayFailures empty). Per /root/.ccr/README.md a 403 from the proxy is a non-retryable organisation egress-policy denial, so no tender detail page, specification or RFT/RFP document could be opened directly. Every opportunity below is therefore captured from WebSearch only: existence / ID / open-status from verifiable result-link <title> text (e.g. 'Current ATM View - <ID>: AusTender', treated as reliable) and any buyer / title / date / scope detail from WebSearch answer snippets (which summarise the target page and are treated as SNIPPET-DERIVED, not independently verified — flagged in each entry's notes and detail_source). Tier 1 Commonwealth (AusTender) and all eight state/territory portals were probed via search: NSW (buy.nsw / eTendering) returned the richest concrete IDs and dates; VIC (Buying for Victoria), QLD (QTenders / supply.qld VendorPanel Marketplace migration), WA (Tenders WA), SA (Tenders SA / Buying4SA) and NT (QTOL) returned mostly landing/portal pages without individual current IDs via search. Tier 2 covered: Sydney/Melbourne/SA Water, NSW Health LHDs, universities (Adelaide, DFAT Quad Infrastructure Fellowships), VendorPanel councils. Tier 3 (mandatory) covered: SAP Business Network Discovery, BHP Find Opportunities, Rio Tinto Buy Local / supplier portals, Fortescue, EstimateOne — all confirmed as buyer-originated portals but with individual opportunities login-/registration-gated, so recorded in discovered_sources rather than fabricated as tenders. Two genuinely new buyer-originated sources were found (WNSW Primary Health Network tenders; Yindjibarndi Energy renewable power offtake EOI).
gaps: EGRESS BLOCKED: all WebFetch calls to external sites returned HTTP 403 EGRESS_BLOCKED (confirmed live against tenders.gov.au). No tender detail pages, specification documents or RFT/RFP attachments could be read. All deliverables/requirements/dates below are snippet-derived from WebSearch and NOT verified against the source notice or its documents.
AusTender (tenders.gov.au) detail pages unreachable — ATM IDs and open-status taken from verifiable WebSearch result titles; scope/close dates from snippets only.

VIC (Buying for Victoria), QLD (QTenders / supply.qld), WA (Tenders WA), SA (Tenders SA / Buying4SA) and NT (QTOL) portals returned only landing/portal pages via WebSearch this run — no individual current opportunity IDs surfaced; these portals require a direct (egress-enabled) fetch to enumerate current tenders.

Tier 3 corporate e-sourcing (SAP Business Network Discovery / SAP Ariba, Coupa, Rio Tinto Buy Local, BHP GCMS) — individual RFx are behind free supplier-account registration or invitation; no authenticated session available, so opportunities were not captured (portals recorded in discovered_sources with access_method=portal-registration). No corporate opportunity was publicly visible without login this run.
Invitation-only corporate/consultancy RFPs (e.g. to Accenture/KPMG/Deloitte) are out of scope and never published — none fabricated.

Several captured opportunities (Tas Derwent Ferry terminals, ACT Aquatic Strategy, ACTPS wellbeing) had no published tender ID in the snippet — dedup keys use a normalised title+buyer instead of an ID and detail is headline-level only.
Some NSW RFT reference numbers (Swansea Bridge BN1365 steel components; NSW RFS GVM upgrades) appeared with slightly conflicting IDs across snippets — treated as uncertain and noted per entry.
recommended_seed_additions: Western NSW Primary Health Network (WNSW PHN) — Tenders — https://wnswphn.org.au/tenders (health, buyer-originated PHN commissioning; not previously known to the routine).

Yindjibarndi Energy — Renewable Energy Power Offtake EOI — https://yindjibarndienergy.com.au/renewable-energy-power-offtake-expressions-of-interest/ (Indigenous-owned energy developer running public EOI processes; note these are power-offtake EOIs, i.e. seeking offtakers/partners, adjacent to but not classic supplier procurement).

AusTender GovPanels / Supplier Portal women-owned business register — the federal Supplier Portal (help.tenders.gov.au/getting-started-with-austender/supplier-portal) opens to all businesses from July 2026 and now includes a publicly searchable women-owned business register; worth monitoring as buyer-discovery shifts (already tracked as a source, flagged here as a material change).

tenders.title: Sydney Water Corporation — Strategic Customer Engagement Program 2026-2029 (Request for Information)
tenders.description: Sydney Water is running a market sounding (RFI) to gather intelligence on market capability, experience and solutions to inform its procurement strategy for the next Strategic Customer Engagement program covering 2026-2029.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Suppliers are asked to describe capability across customer engagement (including deliberative processes), customer research (online surveys, focus groups, forums, in-depth interviews), economics/regulatory specialisation, and diverse and inclusive engagement (First Nations, CALD in-language delivery, financially vulnerable, and people with disability). The buyer's outcome is a procurement strategy and supplier field able to demonstrate that Sydney Water's decision-making, planning and business practices are shaped by and aligned with its customers' and communities' needs. Snippet-derived from the buy.nsw notice summary; RFI document not read (egress-blocked).
key_deliverables: Customer engagement services including deliberative engagement processes
Customer research (online surveys, focus groups, forums, in-depth interviews)
Diverse and inclusive engagement: First Nations, CALD (in-language), financially vulnerable and people with disability

tenders.contract_term: Program period 2026-2029 (RFI is pre-procurement market sounding)
tenders.submission_method: Lodge response via buy.nsw / NSW eTendering

Detail page not fetched (EGRESS_BLOCKED).
tenders.reasoning: Discovered via WebSearch of Sydney Water's next Strategic Customer Engagement program; buyer-originated GBE opportunity published on buy.nsw (NSW eTendering). Not in the routine's known dedup keys.

discovered_sources.source_name: Western NSW Primary Health Network (WNSW PHN) — Tenders
discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch for NSW Health / Local Health District tenders surfaced 'Health Tenders Western & Far West NSW | WNSW PHN' — a Primary Health Network publishing its own commissioning/tender opportunities, distinct from the LHDs and buy.nsw.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated PHN procurement/commissioning page. Not previously in the routine's known-source set (only Adelaide PHN was). PHNs commission health services regionally and are a distinct Tier 2 public-sector channel worth monitoring.

discovered_sources.source_name: Yindjibarndi Energy — Renewable Energy Power Offtake Expressions of Interest
discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch for Australian renewable energy / hydrogen EOIs surfaced Yindjibarndi Energy (Indigenous-owned renewable developer, Pilbara WA) running a public 'Renewable Energy Power Offtake' EOI process.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer/originator-published EOI portal, not an aggregator. Caveat: these are POWER-OFFTAKE EOIs (seeking offtakers/commercial partners for generated power), which is adjacent to — not classic — supplier procurement; still a legitimate market-engagement channel and a seed to find sibling Indigenous/renewable developers running supplier and offtake EOIs.

discovered_sources.source_name: SAP Business Network Discovery (formerly SAP Ariba Discovery)
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Tier 3 mandatory check. WebSearch confirmed SAP Business Network Discovery as the public matchmaking board where buyers post open RFI/RFP/RFQ events (example historical AU post: Energy Queensland protection cubicles).
discovered_sources.notes: Largest single slice of corporate opportunity. Individual open RFx require a free supplier account to view full detail; no authenticated session available this run, so no individual opportunity captured. Recorded here per the mandatory-Tier-3 rule (access=free-registration).

discovered_sources.how_discovered: Tier 3 mandatory check via WebSearch; BHP's supplier 'find opportunities' page confirmed active, with RFQ handled through SAP Ariba Enterprise accounts.
discovered_sources.notes: Opportunities are registration-/invitation-gated via SAP Ariba + GCMS; portal recorded, no individual opportunity fabricated.

discovered_sources.source_name: Rio Tinto — Buy Local EOI Portal
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Tier 3 mandatory check via WebSearch; Rio Tinto Buy Local portal publishes EOIs for goods/services to eligible registered local businesses; major-package EOIs also flagged on the ICN Project portal.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated EOI portal (registration required to respond). Already known to the routine; re-confirmed live this run. Use as a seed for the ICN Project portal for Iron Ore major packages.

discovered_sources.source_name: EstimateOne (E1) — Live Australian commercial construction tenders
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Tier 3 construction check via WebSearch; E1 confirmed as the head-contractor→subcontractor tendering network where Tier-1 builders invite trade quotes.
discovered_sources.notes: Subcontractor work-package invitations are visible to registered subcontractors; no public opportunity captured without a login this run. Builders such as John Holland also run their own e-tendering (TenderLink).

discovered_sources.how_discovered: Tier 2 local-government check via WebSearch; VendorPanel confirmed as the platform hundreds of councils use to publish public tenders (e.g. Logan City Council) and is the target of Queensland's consolidated 'VendorPanel Marketplace' migration.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated council platform (not an aggregator). Queensland is migrating supplier/tender discovery to VendorPanel Marketplace via supply.qld.gov.au — worth watching for QLD local + state consolidation.

discovered_sources.source_name: AusTender GovPanels / Supplier Portal (Commonwealth) — women-owned business register
discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch (sellingtogov.finance.gov.au + help.tenders.gov.au) confirmed the federal Supplier Portal is opening to ALL businesses from July 2026 (from the initial 645 Management Advisory Panel + People Panel suppliers) and now includes a publicly searchable, voluntary women-owned business register.
discovered_sources.notes: Already tracked as a source; flagged as a MATERIAL CHANGE. This is a buyer-discovery (reverse-marketplace) tool — agencies search registered suppliers — rather than a tender-notice feed; it complements, not replaces, AusTender ATMs. The women-owned register and 'all businesses from July 2026' expansion are new this run.
